draft.title: Reproduction in plants, fungi and bacteria
card: Flowering plants
Pollen moves from an anther to a stigma. This is pollination. After fertilisation, the ovule becomes a seed, which can grow into a new plant.
Fungi
Many fungi release spores, tiny cells that grow into new fungi. Yeast, a single-celled fungus, can also reproduce by budding, when a small bud grows on the parent and breaks off.
Bacteria
Bacteria divide by binary fission. The cell copies its DNA, then splits into two new cells.
Spores, budding and binary fission each need only one parent. Seed production in flowering plants usually involves pollen and ovules.
draft.remember: Plants make seeds after pollination, fungi make spores or buds, and bacteria split in two.

a.q: Which process describes how a single bacterial cell reproduces?
opts: It copies its DNA and splits into two cells
It makes spores that grow into new cells
It grows a bud that breaks off the parent
Its pollen fertilises an ovule to make a seed
a.why: Binary fission is when a bacterium copies its DNA and divides into two cells. Spore release is a method used by fungi, so it is the tempting wrong choice, but the card links bacteria to fission.
a.clue: Think about one cell becoming two.

b.q: Priya sees a small bump growing on a yeast cell under a microscope. The bump later breaks away and becomes a new cell. Which process is this?
opts: Budding in a fungus
Binary fission in a bacterium
Pollination in a flowering plant
Spore release in a fungus
b.why: Yeast is a fungus, and a bud that grows on the parent and breaks off is budding. Spore release is also a fungal method, but spores are tiny cells released, not a bump growing on the parent.
b.clue: The new cell grows on the parent first.

a.best: It copies its DNA and splits into two cells

problems.detail: The card says spores 'each need only one parent', but many fungi also make spores sexually (for example zygospores, ascospores and basidiospores), and those come from two parents or mating types. It should say spores 'can' be made by one parent, or limit the claim to asexual spores.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations agree with the card. One problem: the card says spores always need only one parent, which is not true, because many fungi also make spores sexually.
